newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real nudges lower despite stock volatility.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real nudges lower despite stock volatility.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped only 0.06 percent to close at 1.0808 per dollar despite a wave of profit-taking in the stock market that was set off by fears Asian currency woes could spread to Brazil, traders said.
The real's drop in the spot commercial market followed dollar gains in the futures market, leading to arbitrage plays between the spot and future markets, dealers added.
The dollar was driven higher in the futures market by a decision by many players to cover short positions following recent speculative attacks on Asian currencies.
"The spot forex market was calm and only dropped to adjust to a new level in August contracts," one trader said.
Dealers also said a large supply of dollars in the spot market helped keep the market calm amid volatility in stocks and in the market for interest rate futures.
At 1645 local/1945 GMT, preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $170 million surplus.
In the interbank floating-rate market, the real closed at 1.0861 per dollar, 0.01 percent down in quiet trade.
In the parallel market, the real dropped 0.18 percent to end the day at 1.140 per dollar.
